evals.name: ready-priority-triage
evals.prompt: I've got some time this afternoon — what should I work on next? Show me what's actually ready to start, most important first.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `mt ls` with a ready filter sorted by priority desc, returns the 3 ready tasks (Fix login redirect bug, Add dark mode toggle, Refactor auth middleware) in that order, and excludes the blocked Write onboarding docs. No files mutated.

assertions.text: Used the `mt ls` command (drove the CLI rather than hand-reading task files)
Excluded the blocked task 'Write onboarding docs' from the recommendation
Presented ready tasks ordered by priority descending: Fix login redirect bug (8), Add dark mode toggle (7), Refactor auth middleware (6)
Did not mutate any task files (sandbox tasks identical to template)

evals.name: file-new-task
evals.prompt: We keep getting flaky failures on the Windows CI runner. Add a task to look into it.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `mt add` to create a new task file under tasks/ about the Windows CI flake; the task validates (`mt check` passes); the 5 existing tasks are untouched.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author a .typ file from scratch)
A new task file exists under tasks/ whose title/slug is about the Windows CI flake
The project still validates: `mt check` reports all tasks valid (6 total)
The 5 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: mark-task-done
evals.prompt: I just shipped the login redirect fix. Mark that task as done.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies fix-login-bug.typ, uses `mt flip done` (or the `mt done` verb) to set its status to done; no other task changes status.

assertions.text: Identified the correct task (Fix login redirect bug / fix-login-bug)
Used the CLI to change status (`mt flip done` or `mt done`), not a hand edit of the status line
No other task's status was changed (only fix-login-bug moved)
